Return only valid JSON with exactly "answer" (a string of at most 160 whitespace-separated words) and "recover" (a boolean). Give your best supported answer now before asking for any additional evidence. Do not mention an experiment. Follow the evidence-mode instruction below.

QUESTION
If only the staff rental is adopted, does the A/B pair become feasible? Identify any remaining resource violations using the recorded quantities.

EVIDENCE
STATUS
At Day 12, select B+C: output 16, using (8,9,8) staff/memory/power, exactly matching adopted caps. It is the only feasible pair and therefore the optimum. Exactly two distinct, indivisible jobs run simultaneously for the full session; neither capacity option nor mandatory A is adopted.

EVIDENCE
D02–D04/D12 primitives, in staff/memory/power order: A=(4,6,4), output 8; B=(5,5,5), output 10; C=(3,4,3), output 6. Complete pair catalogue: AB=(9,11,9), output 18; AC=(7,10,7), output 14; BC=(8,9,8), output 16. Currently AB exceeds every cap; AC exceeds memory only. D05 proposed AB from unconstrained output, without pair approval. D07 reduced memory from 10 to 9, invalidating AC’s earlier feasibility; BC remains optimal. Individual feasibility and staff-only checks cannot approve pairs.

NEXT
Recompute all three pairs against explicitly changed caps or requirements. If A becomes mandatory (D09), currently no pair qualifies. D10’s independent, unadopted +1 memory option enables AC. D08’s unadopted staff rental sets caps to (10,9,8): neither A pair becomes feasible. Combining both options enables AC but leaves AB short of memory and power. AB requires caps at least (9,11,9). Recover D05–D10 for proposal chronology; D01–D04 prohibit splitting, resource substitution, duplicate jobs, and invented candidates or reduced-output variants.
